<!-- mnthm-1: body_md -->
\label{mnthm:Mainthm}
			Let $\xi$ be the $\operatorname{Pin}^+$ or the $\operatorname{Pin}^-$ structure and let $n$ be an even integer. Then the statement
			\[\text{All }n\text{-dimensional } \xi\text{-manifolds have even Euler characteristic.}\] is true if and only if  $\xi=\operatorname{Pin}^+$ and $n\equiv 2,6\pmod{8}$ or, $\xi=\operatorname{Pin}^-$ and $n\equiv 4\pmod{8}$.
<!-- end mnthm-1 -->
<!-- definition-1: body_md -->
The group $\mathrm{SKK}_n^{\xi}$ is defined by quotienting the monoid of $n$-dimensional $\xi$-manifolds by the relation
			\[M_1\cup M_3+ M_2\cup M_4\sim_{\mathrm{SKK}} M_1\cup M_4+ M_2\cup M_3,\]
			where $M_1, M_2, M_3, M_4$ are compact manifolds the identification of their boundaries $\partial M_1\cong \partial M_2\cong \partial M_3\cong \partial M_4$.
<!-- end definition-1 -->
<!-- mnthm-2: body_md -->
For $n\geq 1$ an odd integer, we have
			\begin{eqnarray*}
			\mathrm{SKK}_n^{Pin^-} &\cong&     \begin{cases}
            \Omega_{n}^{\operatorname{Pin}^-}	&\text{ if } n=1,5,7 \pmod{8}\\
				\Omega_{n}^{\operatorname{Pin}^-}\oplus\mathbb{Z}/2& \text{ if }  n=3 \pmod{8}
			\end{cases}\\
\mathrm{SKK}_n^{Pin^+} &\cong& \begin{cases}
				\Omega_{n}^{\operatorname{Pin}^+}&\text{ if }n=3,7 \pmod{8}\\
				\Omega_{n}^{\operatorname{Pin}^+}\oplus\mathbb{Z}/2& \text{ if }n=5 \pmod{8} 
\end{cases}
            \end{eqnarray*}
            and lastly for $\operatorname{Pin}^+$-manifolds in dimension $n= 1 \pmod{8}$ there is a short exact sequence $\mathbb{Z}/2\to\mathrm{SKK}_n^{\operatorname{Pin}^+}\to \Omega_n^{\operatorname{Pin}^+}$.
<!-- end mnthm-2 -->
<!-- example-1: body_md -->
\label{ex:SmallWu}
		The first few Wu classes are
			\begin{align*}
				&v_1=w_1\\
				&v_2=w_2+w_1^2\\
				&v_3=w_3+\operatorname{Sq}^1(v_2)=w_3+\operatorname{Sq}^1(w_2)=w_2w_1.
			\end{align*}
<!-- end example-1 -->
<!-- lemma-1: body_md -->
\label{lem:EquatioWuWn}
			Let $M^{n}$ be a manifold of dimension $n=2k$. Then $w_n(M)=v_k(M)^2$.
<!-- end lemma-1 -->
<!-- proof-1: body_md -->
This follows directly from the Wu formula \cref{eq:Wuformula}.
<!-- end proof-1 -->
<!-- theorem-1: body_md -->
\cite[{Satz 1}]{dold1956vollstandigkeit}\label{thm:Dold}
			The elements 
			\begin{equation}
				\operatorname{Sq}^{n-k}(p)-v_{n-k}\;p\in H^n(\operatorname{BO};\mathbb{Z}/2)
				\label{eqn:Dold}
			\end{equation}
			for all elements $p\in H^k(\operatorname{BO};\mathbb{Z}/2)$ generate all relations between Stiefel--Whitney numbers of $n$-dimensional manifolds.
<!-- end theorem-1 -->
<!-- lemma-2: body_md -->
\label{lem:EulerCharTopSWClass}
			Let $TM\colon M\to \operatorname{BO}$ be the stable tangent bundle of some closed manifold $M$. Then $\chi(M)\equiv \langle w_n(M),[M]\rangle\pmod{2}$ where $[M]\in H_n(M;\mathbb{Z}/2)$ is the $\mathbb{Z}/2$-fundamental class of manifold $M$.
<!-- end lemma-2 -->
<!-- proposition-1: body_md -->
\label{prop:ConditionEvenEuler}
			Let $\xi\colon B\to \operatorname{BO}$ be any tangential structure. If $w_n\in\xi^*(I_n)\subset H^n(B;\mathbb{Z}/2)$ then all closed $\xi$-manifolds $M^n$ have even Euler characteristic.
<!-- end proposition-1 -->
<!-- proof-2: body_md -->
In this case $w_n(M)$ is trivial for any $n$-dimensional $\xi$-manifold $M$ by  \Cref{thm:Dold}, so by \Cref{lem:EulerCharTopSWClass} $M$ has even Euler characteristic.
<!-- end proof-2 -->
<!-- example-2: body_md -->
We have 
			\begin{enumerate}
            \item $\xi_{w_1} \colon B_{w_1}\to \operatorname{BO}$ is the $BSO$ structure, i.e.\ an orientation
				\item $\xi_{w_2} \colon B_{w_2}\to \operatorname{BO}$ is the $B\operatorname{Pin}^{+}$ structure, $\xi_{\operatorname{Pin}^+}:=\xi_{w_2}$
				\item $\xi_{w_2 + w_1^2} \colon B_{w_2+w_1^{2}} \to \operatorname{BO}$ is the $B\operatorname{Pin}^{-}$ structure, $\xi_{\operatorname{Pin}^-}:=\xi_{w_2+w_1^2}$.
			\end{enumerate}
<!-- end example-2 -->
<!-- notn-1: body_md -->
Let $w\in H^i(\operatorname{BO};\mathbb{Z}/2)$ be a homogeneous cohomology class.
    We denote the ideal generated by actions of the Steenrod algebra $\mathcal{A}$ on $w$ by $(\mathcal{A}w)$. By $(\mathcal{A}w)_n$ we denote its elements in degree $n$, i.e.\ $(\mathcal{A}w)_n = (\mathcal{A}w) \cap H^n(\operatorname{BO};\mathbb{Z}/2)$.
<!-- end notn-1 -->
<!-- lemma-3: body_md -->
\label{lem:betterSets}
			Let $w\in H^i(\operatorname{BO};\mathbb{Z}/2)$ be a homogeneous cohomology class and let $\xi_{w}\colon B_w\to \operatorname{BO}$ be as above. Then  $ \xi_w^*(\langle I_n\cup (\mathcal{A}w)_n \rangle)=\xi_w^*(I_n)$, where $\langle I_n\cup (\mathcal{A}w)_n \rangle \subseteq H^n(BO; \mathbb{Z}/2)$ is the additive subgroup generated by $I_n$ and $(\mathcal{A}w)_n$.
<!-- end lemma-3 -->
<!-- theorem-2: body_md -->
\label{thm:8kp2PinPlus}
			Every $\operatorname{Pin}^+$-manifold in dimension $8k+2$ has even Euler characteristic.
<!-- end theorem-2 -->
<!-- proposition-2: body_md -->
\label{prop:8kp2ToPSWClass}
			Let $n=8k+2$. The universal Stiefel-Whitney class $w_n$ is an element of $\langle I_n\cup (\mathcal{A}w_2)_n\rangle$.
<!-- end proposition-2 -->
<!-- proof-3: body_md -->
Since $w_n\in\langle I_n\cup (\mathcal{A}w_2)_n\rangle$ we can use \Cref{lem:betterSets} to get that $\xi_{\operatorname{Pin}^+}^*(w_n)\in \xi_{\operatorname{Pin}^+}^*(I_n)$. That implies that all $\xi_{\operatorname{Pin}^+}$-manifolds $M$ have $w_n(M)=0$  which suffices to finish the proof using \Cref{prop:ConditionEvenEuler}.
<!-- end proof-3 -->
<!-- lemma-4: body_md -->
\label{lem:SqSWClasses}
			The following formulas hold in $H^*(\operatorname{BO};\mathbb{Z}/2)$.
			\begin{enumerate}
				\item $\operatorname{Sq}^1(w_1^{2i})=0$
				\item $\operatorname{Sq}^2(w_1^{2i})=
				\begin{cases}
					w_1^{2i+2} & 2i\equiv 2,6\pmod{8} \\
					0 & 2i\equiv 0,4\pmod{8}
				\end{cases}$
				\item $\operatorname{Sq}^3(w_1^{2i})=0$
				\item $\operatorname{Sq}^4(w_1^{2i})=\begin{cases}
					w_1^{2i+4} & 2i\equiv 4, 
					6\pmod{8},\\
					0 & 2i \equiv 0,2 \pmod{8}.
				\end{cases}$
			\end{enumerate}
<!-- end lemma-4 -->
<!-- proof-4: body_md -->
The first formula follows from \cref{eqn:Sqw} as
			\[
			\operatorname{Sq}^1(w_1^{2i}) = w_1^i \operatorname{Sq}^1(w_1^i) + \operatorname{Sq}^1(w_1^i) w_1^i = 0.
			\]

			The second formula follows by the first formula using induction on $i$ for
			\begin{align*}
				\operatorname{Sq}^2(w_1^{2i}) &= w_1^2 \operatorname{Sq}^2(w_1^{2i-2}) + \operatorname{Sq}^1(w_1^2) \operatorname{Sq}^1( w_1^{2i-2}) +  \operatorname{Sq}^2(w_1^2) w_1^{2i-2} 
				\\
				&= w_1^2 \operatorname{Sq}^2(w_1^{2i-2}) + w_1^{2i+2}
			\end{align*}
			since $\operatorname{Sq}^2(w_1^2) = w_1^4$.
			
			The third formula follows since
			\[
			\operatorname{Sq}^3(w_1^{2i}) = 2 w_1^i \operatorname{Sq}^3(w_1^{i}) + 2 \operatorname{Sq}^1(w_1^i) \operatorname{Sq}^2(w_1^{i}) = 0.
			\]
			
		
			
			For the final formula, we use $\operatorname{Sq}^4(w_1^2) =  0$, the second formula, and induction after computing
			\begin{align*}
				\operatorname{Sq}^4(w_1^{2i}) &= \operatorname{Sq}^4(w_1^2) w_1^{2i-2} + \operatorname{Sq}^2(w_1^2) \operatorname{Sq}^2(w_1^{2i-2}) + w_1^2 \operatorname{Sq}^4(w_1^{2i-2})
				\\
				&= w_1^4 \operatorname{Sq}^2(w_1^{2i-2}) + w_1^2 \operatorname{Sq}^4(w_1^{2i-2}).
			\end{align*}
			We obtain that $\operatorname{Sq}^4(w_1^{2i}) = 0$ if $2i \equiv 0,2 \mod 8$ and $w_1^{2i+4}$ when $2i \equiv 4,6 \mod 8$.
<!-- end proof-4 -->
<!-- lemma-5: body_md -->
\label{it:4sqprop} Let $i,m$ be nonnegative integers such that $2m+2i\equiv 6\pmod{8}$ then modulo $(\mathcal{A}w_2)$ we have
			\[\operatorname{Sq}^4(w_1^{2i}w_{2m})=w_1^{2i}w_4w_{2m}+
			\begin{cases}
				w_1^{2i}w_{2m+4} & 2i\equiv 0\text{ (mod 8)}\\
				w_1^{2i+2}w_{2m+2} & 2i\equiv 2\text{ (mod 8)}\\
				w_1^{2i+4}w_{2m} & 2i\equiv 4\text{ (mod 8)}\\
				w_1^{2i}w_{2m+4}+w_1^{2i+2}w_{2m+2}+ w_1^{2i+4}w_{2m} & 2i\equiv 6\text{ (mod 8).}
			\end{cases}\]
<!-- end lemma-5 -->
<!-- proof-5: body_md -->
If $2m=2$ then $2i\equiv 4\pmod{8}$ and by the Cartan formula $\operatorname{Sq}^4(w_1^{2i}w_2)\in(\mathcal{A}w_2)$, but in this case also $w_1^{2i}w_4w_{2}+w_1^{2i+4}w_{2}\in (\mathcal{A}w_2)$, hence the formula holds. 
			
			
			Next we assume $2m\geq 4$. We will make the following calculation in $H^*(\operatorname{BO};\mathbb{Z}/2)$ 
			mod $(\mathcal{A}w_2)$, using \Cref{lem:SqSWClasses}, the Cartan formula, \cref{eqn:Sqw} and \cref{tab:binom} of binomial coefficients.
			
			\renewcommand{1.4}{1.4}
			\begin{table}[h!]
				\centering
				\begin{tabular}{c|c|c|c|c|c|c|c|c}
					$i \pmod8=$ & $0$ & $1$ & $2$ & $3$ & $4$ & $5$ & $6$ & $7$ \\ \hline 
					$i\choose 0$&1&1&1&1&1&1&1&1\\ \hline
					$i\choose 1$&0&1&0&1&0&1&0&1\\ \hline
					$i \choose 2$ &$0$&$0$&$1$&$1$&$0$&$0$&$1$&$1$  \\ \hline
					$i \choose 3$ &$0$&$0$&$0$&$1$&$0$&$0$&$0$&$1$ \\ \hline
					$i \choose 4$ &$0$&$0$&$0$&$0$&$1$&$1$&$1$&$1$
				\end{tabular}
				\caption{For convenience of the reader, we collected some binomial coefficients modulo 2. They only depend on $i$ modulo $8$. This follows immediately from Lucas' theorem.}
				\label{tab:binom}
			\end{table}

						\begin{align*}
				&\operatorname{Sq}^4(w_1^{2i}w_{2m})\hspace{.5cm}=\hspace{.5cm}w_1^{2i}\operatorname{Sq}^4(w_{2m})+\operatorname{Sq}^2(w_1^{2i})\operatorname{Sq}^2(w_{2m})+\operatorname{Sq}^4(w_1^{2i})w_{2m}\\
				& = w_1^{2i}\sum_{k=0}^4 {{2m+k-5}\choose{k}}w_{4-k} w_{2m+k}
				+ \operatorname{Sq}^2(w_1^{2i})\sum_{k=0}^2 {{2m+k-3}\choose{k}}w_{2-k} w_{2m+k}
				+\operatorname{Sq}^4(w_1^{2i})w_{2m}\\
				&\stackrel{(w_2\equiv0)}{=}\left(w_1^{2i}w_4w_{2m}+{{2m-1}\choose{4}}w_1^{2i}w_{2m+4}\right)+\operatorname{Sq}^2(w_1^{2i}){{2m-1}\choose{2}}w_{2m+2}+\operatorname{Sq}^4(w_1^{2i})w_{2m} \\
				& = w_1^{2i}w_4w_{2m}+
				\left\{\!\begin{aligned}
					&w_1^{2i}w_{2m+4} &\text{ if }  2m\equiv 0,6\text{ (mod 8)} \\      
					&0 &\text{ if } 2m\equiv 2,4\text{ (mod 8)} 
				\end{aligned}\right\}\\
				&
				+
				\left\{\!\begin{aligned}
					&w_1^{2i+2}w_{2m+2} &\text{ if }  2m\equiv 0,4\text{ (mod 8)} \text{ and } i \text{ odd}\\
					&0 &\text{ if } 2m\equiv 2,6 \text{ (mod 8)}\;\, \text{ or } i \text{ even}  \end{aligned}\right\}
				+ 
				\left\{\!\begin{aligned}
					&w_1^{2i+4}w_{2m} &\text{ if }  2i\equiv 4,6\text{ (mod 8)}\\
					&0 &\text{ if } 2i\equiv 0,2\text{ (mod 8)}      
				\end{aligned}\right\}.
			\end{align*}
			Here we used that $w_2\in (\mathcal{A}w_2)$ and that ${d\choose 1}=0$ and ${d\choose 3}=0 \pmod{2}$ for even $d$.
			
			
			Filling in the condition $2m+2i\equiv 6 \pmod 8$ gives the desired formula.
<!-- end proof-5 -->
<!-- lemma-6: body_md -->
\label{lem:mathfrakR_in_In}
			In $H^*(\operatorname{BO};\mathbb{Z}/2)$ we have that $\mathfrak{r}_{2i}\in I_{8k+2} \;(\text{mod }(\mathcal{A}w_2))$ for all $i$.
<!-- end lemma-6 -->
<!-- proof-6: body_md -->
Using the recursive equation (\ref{eq:RecursiveFormula}) expressing Wu classes in Stiefel-Whitney classes, we calculate that $v_4= w_1^4+w_4 + w_1\operatorname{Sq}^1w_2 + w_2^2  = w_1^4+w_4$ modulo $(\mathcal{A}w_2)$.
			We apply \cref{it:4sqprop} for $2m=8k-2i-2$ and obtain by direct inspection that for any value of $i$ 
			\begin{equation}
				\label{eq:mainRelation}
				\mathfrak{r}_{2i}\equiv \operatorname{Sq}^4(w_1^{2i} w_{8k-2i-2})+v_4w_1^{2i} w_{8k-2i-2} \ \in I_{8k+2} \quad (\text{mod } (\mathcal{A}w_2)).
			\end{equation}
<!-- end proof-6 -->
<!-- proof-7: body_md -->
We compute
			\begin{align*}
				\sum_{i=0}^{4k-1}\mathfrak{r}_{2i}&=
				\sum_{j=0}^{k-1} (\mathfrak{r}_{8j} +\mathfrak{r}_{8j+2} + \mathfrak{r}_{8j+4} + \mathfrak{r}_{8j+6}) 
				\\
				&=\sum_{j=0}^{k-1}w_1^{8j}(w_{8k+2-8j}+w_1^{8j+4}w_{8k-2-8j}+ w_1^{8j+4}w_{8k-8k-2}+w_1^{8k+6}w_{8k-4-8k}\\&\hspace{10mm} +w_1^{8j+6}w_{8k-8j-4}+w_1^{8j+8}w_{8k-8j-6})\\
				&= \sum_{j=0}^{k-1}(w_1^{8j}w_{8k+2-8j} + w_1^{8j+8}w_{8k-6-8j})
				\\
				&= w_{8k+2} + w_1^{8k} w_{2}
			\end{align*}
			
			By \Cref{lem:mathfrakR_in_In}, the elements $\mathfrak{r_{2i}}\in I_n$ and so $\sum_{i=0}^{4k-1}\mathfrak{r}_{2i}\in I_n$. It follows that $w_{8k+2}\in  I_n \pmod{(\mathcal{A} w_2)}$.
<!-- end proof-7 -->
<!-- proposition-3: body_md -->
\label{prop:PinMinusEulerChar} 
			Every $Pin^-$ manifold of dimension $8k+4$ has vanishing top Wu class $v_{4k+2}$ and therefore even Euler characteristic.
<!-- end proposition-3 -->
<!-- lemma-7: body_md -->
\label{lm:SqForPinMinus}
			For every integer $k>0$ we have:
			\[\operatorname{Sq}^{4k+2}=\operatorname{Sq}^2\operatorname{Sq}^{4k}+\operatorname{Sq}^2\operatorname{Sq}^{4k-1}\operatorname{Sq}^{1}.\]
<!-- end lemma-7 -->
<!-- proof-8: body_md -->
Recall the Adem relations for Steenrod squares:
		\begin{equation}\label{eq:Adem}
			\operatorname{Sq}^a \operatorname{Sq}^b
			=
			\sum_{j=0}^{\lfloor a/2\rfloor}
			\binom{b-j-1}{a-2j}
			\operatorname{Sq}^{a+b-j}\operatorname{Sq}^j,
			\qquad \text{for } a<2b.
		\end{equation}
		
            In particular we have that
			\[\operatorname{Sq}^{2}\operatorname{Sq}^{4k}={4k-1\choose 2}\operatorname{Sq}^{4k+2}+{4k-2\choose 0}\operatorname{Sq}^{4k+1}\operatorname{Sq}^{1}=\operatorname{Sq}^{4k+2}+\operatorname{Sq}^{4k+1}\operatorname{Sq}^{1},\]
			so we obtain that $\operatorname{Sq}^{4k+2} = \operatorname{Sq}^{2}\operatorname{Sq}^{4k}+\operatorname{Sq}^{4k+1}\operatorname{Sq}^{1}$. By another Adem relation:
			$$\operatorname{Sq}^2\operatorname{Sq}^{4k-1}={4k-2\choose 2}\operatorname{Sq}^{4k+1}+{4k-3\choose 0}\operatorname{Sq}^{4k}\operatorname{Sq}^{1}=\operatorname{Sq}^{4k+1}+\operatorname{Sq}^{4k}\operatorname{Sq}^1,$$ we get $ \operatorname{Sq}^2\operatorname{Sq}^{4k-1}=\operatorname{Sq}^{4k+1}+\operatorname{Sq}^{4k}\operatorname{Sq}^{1}$, which we precompose by $\operatorname{Sq}^1$ to obtain
			
			\[\operatorname{Sq}^2\operatorname{Sq}^{4k-1}\operatorname{Sq}^1=\operatorname{Sq}^{4k+1}\operatorname{Sq}^1+\operatorname{Sq}^{4k}\operatorname{Sq}^{1}\operatorname{Sq}^1.\]
			  A simple application of another Adem relation gives  $Sq^1 Sq^1 = 0$ and we can calculate.
			\[\operatorname{Sq}^{4k+2} = \operatorname{Sq}^{2}\operatorname{Sq}^{4k}+\operatorname{Sq}^{4k+1}\operatorname{Sq}^{1} = \operatorname{Sq}^{2}\operatorname{Sq}^{4k}+\operatorname{Sq}^2\operatorname{Sq}^{4k-1}\operatorname{Sq}^1\]
			which concludes the proof.
<!-- end proof-8 -->
<!-- proof-9: body_md -->
A manifold $M^n$ admits a tangential $\xi_{\operatorname{Pin}^{-}}$-structure if and only if the second Wu class $v_2(M)=w_1^2+w_2$ is zero, hence for any $x\in H^{n-2}(M;\mathbb{Z}/2)$, we have
        $    Sq^2(x) = v_2(M) x =0.$
                    For $n=8k+4$ and any $y\in H^{4k+2}(M;\mathbb{Z}/2)$, 
            \[
            v_{4k+2}(M)y = \operatorname{Sq}^{4k+2}(y)= \operatorname{Sq}^2 \left(\operatorname{Sq}^{4k} + \operatorname{Sq}^{4k+1}\operatorname{Sq}^1 \right)(y) = 0,
            \]
using \Cref{lm:SqForPinMinus}, hence it follows that $v_{4k+2}(M)$ vanishes. Finally, since $w_{8k+4}(M)=v_{4k+2}(M)^2$ we get that $w_{8k+4}(M)=0$ for all $\xi_{\operatorname{Pin}^-}$-manifolds $M$ and thus by \Cref{prop:ConditionEvenEuler} all $Pin^-$-manifolds have even Euler characteristic.
<!-- end proof-9 -->
<!-- proposition-4: body_md -->
\label{prop:pinplusdim6}
			Every $\operatorname{Pin}^+$ manifold of dimension $n=8k+6$ has vanishing top Wu class $v_{4k+3}$ and therefore even Euler characteristic.
<!-- end proposition-4 -->
<!-- proof-10: body_md -->
A manifold $M^n$ admits a tangential $\xi_{\operatorname{Pin}^{+}}$-structure if and only if $w_2(M)=0$. We have $v_3 = w_1 w_2$, so $\xi_{\operatorname{Pin}^+}^* (v_3)=0$, from which it follows that $\operatorname{Sq}^3(x) = 0$ for any $x\in H^{n-3}(M;\mathbb{Z}/2)$.
By an Adem relation (\ref{eq:Adem}), we have for $k\geq 0$
			$$\operatorname{Sq}^{4k+3} = \operatorname{Sq}^3 \operatorname{Sq}^{4k}.$$
Let $n=8k+6$, and $y\in H^{4k+3}(M;\mathbb{Z}/2)$, then
  \[v_{4k+3}(M)y=\operatorname{Sq}^{4k+3}(y)=\operatorname{Sq}^3 \operatorname{Sq}^{4k}(y)=0,\]
  hence $v_{4k+3}=0$ and therefore $w_{8k+3}(M)=v_{4k+3}(M)^2=0$, thus all $(8k+6)$-dimensional $Pin^+$-manifolds have even Euler characteristic.
<!-- end proof-10 -->
<!-- theorem-3: body_md -->
\label{thm:TheExactSequence}
			Let $\xi\colon B\to \operatorname{BO}$ be a stable tangential structure.
			Then the canonical map $\mathrm{SKK}^\xi_n \to \Omega^{\xi}_n$ is well-defined and yields an exact sequence
			\begin{equation} \label{seq:theSesSKK}
				\begin{tikzcd}
					0\ar[r]&\langle S_b^n \rangle_{\mathrm{SKK}^\xi_n} \ar[r,"s"]&\mathrm{SKK}_n^{\xi}\ar[r]& \Omega^\xi_n \ar[r]& 0,
				\end{tikzcd}
			\end{equation}
			where $\langle S^n_b\rangle$ is a cyclic group and the map $s$ sends a generator to the sphere $S^n$ with the unique $\xi$-structure that extends to the disk $D^{n+1}$.
			
			If $n$ is even $\langle S_b^n \rangle_{\mathrm{SKK}^\xi_n} \cong \mathbb{Z}$, and if $n$ is odd then
			\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
				\item \label{it:ses1}$[S^n_b] = 0 \in \mathrm{SKK}^\xi_n$ if there exists a closed $(n+1)$-dimensional $\xi$-manifold with odd Euler characteristic;
				\item\label{it:ses2}$\langle S_b^n \rangle_{\mathrm{SKK}^\xi_n} \cong \mathbb{Z}/2$ if all closed $(n+1)$-dimensional $\xi$-manifolds have even Euler characteristic.
			\end{enumerate}
<!-- end theorem-3 -->
<!-- corollary-1: body_md -->
\label{cor:SKKPin}
			 Let $n\geq 1$ be an odd integer and let $\xi$ be $B\operatorname{Pin}^{+}\to \operatorname{BO}$ or $B\operatorname{Pin}^{-}\to \operatorname{BO}$. Then we get that 
			\begin{eqnarray*}
			\mathrm{SKK}_n^{Pin^-} &\cong&     \begin{cases}
            \Omega_{n}^{\operatorname{Pin}^-}	&\text{ if } n=1,5,7 \pmod{8}\\
				\Omega_{n}^{\operatorname{Pin}^-}\oplus\mathbb{Z}/2& \text{ if }  n=3 \pmod{8}
			\end{cases}\\
\mathrm{SKK}_n^{Pin^+} &\cong& \begin{cases}
				\Omega_{n}^{\operatorname{Pin}^+}&\text{ if }n=3,7 \pmod{8}\\
				\Omega_{n}^{\operatorname{Pin}^+}\oplus\mathbb{Z}/2& \text{ if }n=5 \pmod{8} 
\end{cases}
            \end{eqnarray*}
            and lastly for $\operatorname{Pin}^+$-manifolds in dimension $n= 1 \pmod{8}$ there is a short exact sequence $\mathbb{Z}/2\to\mathrm{SKK}_n^{\operatorname{Pin}^+}\to \Omega_n^{\operatorname{Pin}^+}$.
    
            In the above the $\mathbb{Z}/2$ summands are generated by the spheres $S^n_b$ with $\xi$-structures which extend to the $n+1$-disc. The maps $\mathrm{SKK}_n^{\xi}\to \Omega_n^{\xi}$ are given by the inclusion and in the split cases the map $\mathrm{SKK}^{\xi}_n\to \mathbb{Z}/2$ is given by the $\mathbb{Z}/2$-Kervaire semi-characteristic
            \[\operatorname{kerv}_{\mathbb{Z}/2}(M^{2k+1})=\sum_{i=0}^{k}\operatorname{rank}(H_i(M;\mathbb{Z}/2)).\]
<!-- end corollary-1 -->
<!-- proof-11: body_md -->
That $\mathrm{SKK}^{\xi}_n$ is isomorphic to either a bordism group or to an extension of the bordism group by $\mathbb{Z}/2$ follows from \Cref{mnthm:Mainthm} and \Cref{thm:TheExactSequence}. The fact that in the $8k+5$ dimensional $\operatorname{Pin}^+$ case and the $8k+3$ dimensional $\operatorname{Pin}^-$ case is split by the Kervaire semi-characteristic follows from \cite[Theorem B]{HSV2025} since in \Cref{prop:pinplusdim6} and \Cref{prop:PinMinusEulerChar} we show that in those cases the top Wu classes vanish.
<!-- end proof-11 -->
<!-- lemma-8: body_md -->
\label{lem:Pin+counterexamples}
            In every dimension $n=8k+2$ there exists a $\operatorname{Pin}^+$ manifold $M^{8k+2}$ such that $v_{4k+1}(M)\neq 0$, even though $w_{8k+2}(M)=0$.
<!-- end lemma-8 -->
<!-- proof-12: body_md -->
Consider the manifold  $M:=K^2\times \mathbb{HP}^{2k}$ where $K^2$ is the Klein bottle. Now $w_2(M)= w_2(K)+ w_1(K) w_1(\mathbb{HP}^{2k}) + w_2(\mathbb{HP}^{2k}) = w_2(K)$ which vanishes since $w_2(K)=\chi(K)\pmod{2}=0$. Now $v_{4k+1}(M)=  v_1(K)v_{4k}(\mathbb{HP}^{2k})$. Since $\chi(\mathbb{HP}^{2k})$ is nonzero, $w_{8k}(\mathbb{HP}^{2k})\neq 0$ and so $v_{4k}(\mathbb{HP})\neq 0$. Furthermore $w_1(K)=v_1(K)\neq 0$ which proves  the claim.
<!-- end proof-12 -->
<!-- question-1: body_md -->
Does the exact sequence
    \begin{equation}\label{eq:Pinskk}
            0 \to \mathbb{Z}/2 \to \mathrm{SKK}^{\operatorname{Pin}^+}_{8k+1} \to \Omega^{\operatorname{Pin}^+}_{8k+1} \to 0
        \end{equation}

    split for all $k \geq 0$?
<!-- end question-1 -->
<!-- lemma-9: body_md -->
If there exists a $k$ for which \cref{eq:Pinskk} does not split, then for any $k'\geq k$, it also does not split.
<!-- end lemma-9 -->
<!-- proof-13: body_md -->
If for an integer $k$  \cref{eq:Pinskk}
    is not split then there exists a manifold $X^{8k+1}$ with the property that $2[X]=[S_b^{8k+1}]$ in $\mathrm{SKK}^{\operatorname{Pin}^+}_{8k+1}$. Let $k'>k$. Consider the manifold $X'= X \times \mathbb{HP}^{2(k'-k)}$. Let $W$ be a nullbordism of $X \sqcup X$. Using \cite[Lemma 3.13]{HSV2025} we have that in $\mathrm{SKK}^{\operatorname{Pin}^+}_{8k+1}$
    \[2[X]=\chi(W)[S^{8k+1}]\]
    and so $\chi(W)\equiv 1\pmod{2}$. Then $W\times \mathbb{HP}^{2(k'-k)}$ is a nullbordism of $X'\sqcup X'$ and using the same result we have that in $\mathrm{SKK}^{\operatorname{Pin}^+}_{8k'+1}$
    \[
    [X' \sqcup X'] = \chi(W)\chi(\mathbb{HP}^{2(k'-k)})[S_b^{8k'+1}] \equiv [S_b^{8k'+1}],
    \]
    which proves the result.
<!-- end proof-13 -->
